title: How to Merge PDF Files Safely and Keep Pages in Order
description: Learn how to combine PDF files, arrange page order, check the merged document and understand what may not be preserved.
intro: Combining PDFs is useful for reports, applications and project handoffs. Before merging, decide the order, keep original copies and review the final document for pages and features that matter.

sections.heading: Prepare the source PDFs
paragraphs: Rename files clearly or make a short list of the intended order. Check that each source opens correctly and that you have permission to combine and share its contents.
Keep the originals unchanged. A merged PDF is a new output, and retaining the source files makes it easier to correct ordering or replace one part later.

sections.heading: Arrange files in reading order
paragraphs: A common order is cover, contents, main sections, appendices and supporting material. The right order depends on the reader and the purpose of the document.
Use the preview and reorder controls to put pages in sequence before processing. For a large merge, inspect section boundaries and make sure a page was not omitted or duplicated.

sections.heading: Check the merged document
paragraphs: After merging, open the output and review the first and last pages, section transitions, page orientation and any pages with unusual sizes. If a page contains a form, signature or link, check whether it remains usable.

PDF merge tools may preserve page content while not carrying every interactive feature, such as forms, signatures, bookmarks or document-level metadata. Do not assume these features survive unchanged; test the output that you plan to distribute.

sections.heading: Merge locally with iLoveMyFiles
paragraphs: Open the Merge PDF tool, choose the files, arrange their order, then process and download the combined document. The tool runs in your browser; large files may use significant device memory, so close other heavy tabs if processing is slow.
For a different task, use Split PDF to separate pages, or Compress PDF to create a smaller copy. Always verify the result before sending it on.

faq.question: Can I change page order before merging?
faq.answer: Yes. Arrange source files or pages in the required sequence before processing, then review the finished PDF.

faq.question: Will merging change my original files?
faq.answer: The merge creates a separate output; keep the source PDFs if you need to repeat or change the merge.

faq.question: Do bookmarks, signatures and forms always survive?
faq.answer: No. Interactive and document-level features may not be preserved by every PDF library. Inspect and test the output before relying on them.

faq.question: Are my PDFs sent to a server?
faq.answer: The Merge PDF tool processes files in your browser. Review the tool page for current details and browser memory limitations.
